Below is the full 12‑week programme summary for your client (29 y/o recreational climber, right subacromial impingement ~4 months into physio). It integrates upper‑body strength (pain‑aware), progressive hangboard and climbing prep, two cardio sessions/week for endurance, mobility and rotator‑cuff work, nutrition for body recomposition, a Saturday full‑body “finisher,” and a Phase C push peak so she arrives fresh and strong for her week‑12 climbing trip. Follow the pain rules strictly: no sharp/pinch pain, only pain‑free ranges, and consult her physio before progressing hangs, overhead‑like loading, or any new shoulder stress.

High‑level structure
- Duration: 12 weeks, 3 strength sessions/week (Sessions A, B, C).
- Cardio: 2 sessions/week (Cardio 1 = steady Zone 2; Cardio 2 = climbing‑specific intervals/long).
- Hangboard: introduced late — conservative start in Weeks 7–8 (Phase B), progressive in Phase C (Weeks 9–12) only with physio clearance.
- Mobility & rotator cuff: daily short routine + 2–3 fuller sessions/week.
- Saturday Finisher: weekly fun full‑body session (25–40 min).
- Nutrition: body recomposition approach — mild average calorie deficit (~−200–300 kcal/day), protein 1.8–2.2 g/kg, carbs adjusted for training days, creatine recommended.
- Progression: three phases — Foundation (Weeks 1–4), Strength (Weeks 5–8), Strength/Transfer + Peak (Weeks 9–12). Autoregulate by pain and RPE; increase loads conservatively.

Pain & safety rules (repeat)
- No sharp/pinch pain during or after exercises. Mild muscular ache acceptable if baseline and resolves.
- No overhead barbell presses or end‑range overhead loading on symptomatic side unless physio clears and pain‑free.
- Avoid full dead‑hangs early; keep elbow flexed and use assistance.
- If pain ↑ or impingement reproduced, regress to more supportive variations (chest‑supported rows, floor press, landmine presses) and check with physio.

Weekly template (typical microcycle)
- Mon: Strength Session A (Horizontal push/pull emphasis; push power in Phase C)
- Tue: Cardio 1 (Zone 2 steady) + optional short hangboard in Phase C as scheduled
- Wed: Strength Session B (Pull emphasis + carries)
- Thu: Mobility / recovery or easy climbing technique
- Fri: Strength Session C (Push alternatives + scapular / rotator cuff + climbing transfer)
- Sat: Cardio 2 (climbing intervals or long steady) + Saturday Finisher
- Sun: Easy climbing (low intensity) or rest — practice technique if no pain

Phase A — Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
Goal: build scapular control, rotator cuff endurance, pain‑free horizontal pulling/pushing, and thoracic mobility.

Key points
- Higher rep ranges (8–12), controlled tempo, emphasis on technique and rotator cuff.
- No hangboard work. Cardio: 2 low‑impact Zone 2 sessions/week (25–40 min).
- Daily mobility warm‑ups and post‑session cooldowns.

Session A (example)
- Warm‑up 10–15 min (bike + shoulder dynamic)
- Rotator cuff/scapular activation: wall slides, side‑lying ER, serratus punches
- Main: TRX/body rows 4 × 8–12; floor/incline neutral DB press 3 × 8–12
- Accessory: single‑arm cable row 3 × 10 each; farmer carry 3 × 40 m
- Cooldown: band pull‑aparts 3 × 15; pec stretch

Session B (example)
- Main: seated cable row 4 × 8–12; landmine single‑arm press 3 × 8–10 (low angle)
- Accessory: eccentric‑focused lat negatives 3 × 6–8; scaption 3 × 12
- Core: plank variations

Session C (example)
- Main: chest‑supported row 4 × 8–12; dumbbell floor/incline press 3 × 8–10
- Accessory: TRX T‑holds 3 × 5–8s; eccentric one‑arm lat 3 × 6
- Core: Pallof press 3 × 10 each

Phase B — Strength (Weeks 5–8)
Goal: increase absolute pulling strength and single‑arm work; begin conservative climbing specificity late in this phase.

Key points
- Rep ranges shift to ~6–8 for main lifts. Maintain rotator cuff volume.
- Cardio: longer Zone 2 sessions; Cardio 2 includes intervals.
- Hangboard intro: ONLY in Weeks 7–8 after physio clearance and pain‑free status.

Session A (example)
- Chest‑supported row or bent‑over neutral row 4 × 6–8 (choose chest‑supported if shoulder sensitive)
- Neutral DB floor press 4 × 6–8
- Farmer carry/rack carry 3 × 40–60 m

Session B (example)
- Assisted pull‑ups or neutral lat pulldown 4 × 6–8 (partial ROM if needed)
- Single‑arm DB row 3 × 6–8 each
- Scapular retraction holds / eccentric negatives 3 sets

Session C (example)
- Incline neutral DB press 4 × 6–8
- TRX/body row heavy 4 × 6–8
- Single‑arm landmine row 3 × 8 each

Phase C — Strength & Transfer + Push Peak (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: heavier single‑arm pulling and pushing work, hangboard progression, climbing endurance simulation, and peak push intensity for week 12 trip. Taper in final week.

Key points
- Main lifts: 3–6 rep range for strength; maintain accessories 6–12.
- Hangboard sessions twice weekly — progressive repeaters and short near‑max hangs only if pain‑free.
- Cardio: longer Zone 2 sessions and climbing simulation sessions; build to longer durations (60–90 min as tolerated).
- Push progression: heavy single‑arm landmine presses, neutral dumbbell floor presses, explosive push‑ups and medicine‑ball work. Peak in week 12 with reduced volume (taper).
- Mobility continued daily; reduce volume of mobility during taper week but keep activation.

Push progression (Weeks 9–12 summary)
- Weeks 9–10: Single‑arm landmine press 4 × 5; floor press 4 × 5–6; explosive push‑ups 4 × 6
- Week 11: Increase single‑arm landmine 5 × 3–4; floor press 4 × 4–6; power work 5 × 3–5
- Week 12 (taper): Heavy but low volume: landmine 3 × 3 per arm; floor press 3 × 4; explosive push‑ups 3 × 3–4. Reduce accessory volume ~30–40%.

Hangboard progression (Phase B end → Phase C)
- Weeks 7–8 (intro):
  - Assisted repeaters on large jugs: 3 rounds × 6–8 repeats (7s hang : 3s rest), feet on box for 25–40% offload.
  - Short assisted isometrics 4–6 × 5–8s on large holds.
- Weeks 9–10 (level 2):
  - Repeaters 6–8 × 10s hang :5s rest × 3–4 rounds with partial assistance.
  - 4–6 short near‑max holds 7–10s with full recovery (assisted on symptomatic side).
  - Climbing prep: route linking intervals 30–45 min.
- Weeks 11–12 (level 3):
  - Endurance repeaters and short max holds; total session hang time increases progressively to ~12–20 min depending on tolerance.
  - Long climbing simulation: 60–120 min blocks to mimic long days; practice nutrition and pacing.
- Always log hold used, assistance amount, pain before/during/after.

Cardio plan (2×/wk) — progression overview
- Cardio 1: steady Zone 2 (bike/elliptical/incline walk) — start 25–40 min (Phase A) → 35–75 min (Phase C).
- Cardio 2: climbing‑specific intervals or long steady sessions:
  - Phase A: 30–45 min with short technique blocks.
  - Phase B: 35–55 min with intervals (3–5 min efforts).
  - Phase C: 50–90 min long sessions or climbing simulation blocks.
- Avoid modalities that aggravate shoulder (rower only if pain‑free; swimming only with physio clearance and short strokes).

Mobility & rotator cuff program (daily + 2–3 fuller sessions/week)
- Daily warm‑up (8–12 min): light cardio, thoracic rotations, band pull‑aparts, scapular push‑ups, band ER.
- Post‑session cooldown (5–10 min): pec minor stretch, posterior capsule/cross‑body stretch, lat stretch, rotator cuff isometrics.
- Full mobility sessions (15–25 min): soft‑tissue work (pec/lat), thoracic extension drills, wall angels or supine scapular slides, prone T/Y, band face pulls, serratus punches, Pallof press.
- Travel routine: ~10 min activation and mobility to do at the crag/hotel.

Saturday Finisher (weekly; scalable)
- Duration: 25–40 min. Circuit (3–4 rounds) or AMRAP.
- Example Circuit: kettlebell swings 12; single‑arm landmine pushes 8 each; TRX inverted rows 10; farmer carry 40–60 m; med‑ball rotational toss 12 each; grip endurance 30–45s.
- Progression: increase rounds/weight/intervals across phases; include assisted hangs in Phase C only if pain‑free.
- Taper finisher volume in week 12.

Nutrition — body recomposition (summary)
- Goal: mild weekly calorie deficit (−200 to −300 kcal average) while preserving/building muscle.
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day; fats ~25–30% calories; carbs fill remainder with more on training days.
- Training days: near‑maintenance calories; rest days slightly lower.
- Peri‑workout: 20–40 g carbs + 10–30 g protein pre; 20–40 g protein + 30–60 g carbs post.
- Supplements (optional): creatine 3–5 g/day; whey or plant protein; omega‑3 if low fish intake; vitamin D if low levels.
- Monitor: weekly bodyweight, waist measurement, training performance. Adjust calories by ~100 kcal if progress too fast/slow.

Recovery & taper guidance
- Sleep 7–9 hours; prioritize sleep in weeks 10–12.
- Reduce total training volume by ~30–50% in the last 7–10 days before the trip for freshness; keep intensity on key lifts but cut accessory and finisher volume.
- If shoulder soreness appears during taper, reduce hang and push intensity further and emphasize mobility and physio input.

Logging & metrics to track
- Training: exercise, sets/reps/load, RPE, pain score (0–10) before/during/24–48h after session.
- Hangboard: hold, assistance (% BW), total hang time.
- Cardio: modality, duration, HR or RPE, session notes.
- Nutrition: daily calories, protein, weight once weekly.
- Mobility: subjective ROM improvement and pain levels.
